name: atlas-hydro-dss
description: Decision-support system for drought & drinking-water stress in Morocco's Béni Mellal–Khénifra region: live Copernicus/ECMWF data, Pydantic QA, DuckDB, PuLP optimisation and a bilingual Streamlit dashboard with an animated 3D basin story.

paragraphs: A decision-support system that explains why taps run dry in the Oum Er-Rbia basin, who is affected, and what each solution would change. It takes live satellite and reanalysis data, checks every record, and runs two optimisation models. Everything is shown in a bilingual (EN/FR) dashboard, including an animated 3D story of the basin.

🌐 Live app: atlas-water.streamlit.app. It is free-hosted, so after a quiet period the first visit can take a minute or two while it wakes up. 📄 Full analysis: docs/REPORT.md. It covers the diagnosis, the scenario results, the effect of each solution, and recommendations.
From 2018 to 2025 Morocco went through seven dry years. The Oum Er-Rbia basin fell to 4.4% of its dam capacity (Sept 2024), and Al Massira, the country's second-largest dam, to 0.4%.
features: farmers whose wells went from 20 m to 40 m deep.
What are citizens and farmers actually facing? 18 documented problems, 6 citizen testimonies and an impact map, all sourced.

Why? Reanalysis data shows that the 2020–2025 drought cut rainfall by 22% but river inflow by 63%. The cause is +2.0 °C of warming and 70% less snow, made worse by over-pumped aquifers and towns that depend on a single…
